info.title: Price Monitor API
info.description: API for tracking diesel, Brent crude, and bitumen prices. In team mode, business data, history, and exports are private. Viewer: read/export; editor: write/collect; administrator: accounts/audit/metrics. Local personal development allows loopback access without an account.

get.summary: Diesel, Brent, and bitumen index forecasts

200.description: Prices at 7/30/90 days and BLS bitumen index at 1/3/6 months from the latest source date. Each product exposes its unit, frequency, horizons, persistence comparison, historical coverage, and calibrated intervals. Intervals at longer horizons use a non-overlapping historical stress envelope when sufficient evidence exists; otherwise they are withheld.

403.description: Invalid origin, HTTPS, CSRF, or insufficient permission

get.description: Brent and diesel forecasts use only spot series, with stable FRED, EIA, then Alpha Vantage priority. Futures and the heating oil proxy are excluded from this history. One point per source date is selected before limiting; the latest 5,000 aggregated points are kept in chronological order. Each selected endpoint is persisted once with its model version, original baseline, and interval.

200.description: Persisted issued forecasts, their resolved actuals, rolling MAE/RMSE/MAPE, bias, improvement over the original last-known-price baseline, and interval coverage with a 95% target, gap, and monitoring status.

403.description: Invalid origin, HTTPS, CSRF, or insufficient permission

get.description: Scores only the same instrument: a futures or heating-oil observation can never resolve a spot forecast. Daily targets accept the first published actual on the target date through four days later; the monthly BLS index requires the target month. When product, instrument, and horizon are supplied, the current production candidate is reported rather than mixing it with shadow forecasts.

get.summary: Versioned forecast candidates and lifecycle audit

200.description: Production and shadow candidates, version identities, promotion and rollback criteria including interval coverage, and append-only lifecycle events.

403.description: Invalid origin, HTTPS, CSRF, or insufficient permission

get.description: Candidates are versioned, first run in shadow against identical issued endpoints, and are promoted only after 30 paired actuals and at least 5% MAE improvement. A non-persistence model rolls back after 30 live actuals when its MAE is more than 10% worse than its issued persistence baseline.
